L0_source_surface.claim: virtual assistant answers can be pulled from a knowledge graph; graphs represent semantic information between entities.
a knowledge graph is made of nodes connected by edges; nodes describe objects/persons/places and edges define relationships.

L1_conceptual.claim: the same pair of nodes can have multiple relationship edges, e.g. Paris as capital of France and city of Roman Empire.

L2_information_structure.claim: knowledge graphs bind different data sources together and can infer missing facts beyond one incomplete/outdated data source.
NLP can classify unstructured text and perform semantic enrichment to create correlated datasets and a knowledge graph.

L3_context_background.claim: commercial applications include Q&A, YouTube recommendations, insurance fraud checks, and retail product relations.

L4_emotional_rhetorical.claim: the speaker uses familiarity and everyday assistant examples to reduce technical distance.
the coffee/sleep example uses humor to make node-edge modeling memorable.

L5_power_authority.claim: platforms and companies use knowledge graphs to steer recommendations, claims, and retail pairings; this carries commercial decision power.

L6_practical_operational.claim: an operational pipeline is implied: unstructured text -> NLP classification -> semantic enrichment -> correlated datasets -> knowledge graph.

L7_counter_uncertainty.claim: single data sources may be outdated or misclassified, so graph inference depends on data quality and source integration.

L8_vectorfl_mapping.claim: supports VectorFL mini-space structure: meaning arises from explicit relationships between entities rather than isolated notes.
